scorecard.rationale: The uncontrolled 14-person Parkinson brewed-green-tea pilot reports mean fatigue increasing from 28.4 to 32.1 and higher medians, with no paired variance or exact fatigue p value. Opposing evidence includes a postoperative whole-tea comparison and customary relief of tiredness. Some isolated caffeine and caffeine–theanine contrasts favor lower task fatigue. Controlled withdrawal comparisons suggest that short abstention can contribute to that signal. The usual-diet cycling outcome showed no caffeine condition effect and the taper trials do not report a separate fatigue contrast. The acute comparisons do not replicate a prepared green-tea Parkinson exposure. The closest pilot retains a tentative worsening lean. Controlled brewed-tea Parkinson results and the remaining original measures stay open. An isolated catechin crossover in multiple sclerosis reported exercise efficiency and metabolic differences, with no dedicated fatigue result. A separate signaling review supplies EGCG constituent context, not a beverage fatigue measure. Neither changes the closest brewed tea pilot's tentative worsening signal. The added flavonoid review covers catechins and EGCG. Its fatigue example instead concerns quercetin treatment in an oncology setting. Keep the original brewed-green-tea evidence separate.
